errors.text: The hypothesis does not identify the required critical threshold of approximately 900 K, instead tying the transition to an unmeasured stacking-fault-energy sign reversal extrapolated from a different alloy where the crossing occurs near 260 K.

It replaces the observed mediator—stable dislocation density at 300–600 K followed by a substantial density reduction and rapid disorder at 900–1200 K—with an unsupported dislocation-avalanche mechanism.
Suppression of stacking faults and fcc-to-hcp transformation conflicts with the target observation that the HCP atom fraction increases with temperature.
Evidence from CoCrFeMnNi and bcc MoNbTaW does not establish temperature-dependent stacking-fault energy or kink-pair-controlled deformation in FeNiCrCoCu on Cu.
